name: The Test-Suite Organizer
oneLiner: Bulk-organizes an ADO test suite — files test cases into suites, repairs broken TestedBy links, normalizes titles to a naming convention, and reassigns testers.
lead: A team keeps hundreds of test cases organized in suites under an ADO Test Plan. This agent maintains that structure at scale: it adds test cases to suites, audits each for a missing or reversed `TestedBy` link to its parent story, normalizes titles to the `TC_US<storyId>_` convention, and drives tester ownership across the work item, the test case, and its test point.
chore: By hand, keeping a suite tidy is soul-crushing. Someone opens suite after suite, checks each test case's title against the convention, confirms it's linked to the right story in the right direction, and records its owner — across hundreds of items. Titles drift, links point the wrong way, and reassigning work when someone leaves means editing dozens of items one at a time.
instead: The agent does the whole sweep in one pass. It lists suite contents, adds test cases, and — most usefully — audits every case for three defects: a missing `TestedBy-Reverse` link, a reversed (`TestedBy-Forward`) link, and a title that breaks the naming convention. It reports each, and on approval fixes them. It also reads a feature's stories to auto-assign each test case to its author, and bulk-reassigns ownership when it changes.
whyItMatters: When every test case is filed, named, and owned correctly, a lead can trust the Test Plan at a glance instead of second-guessing whether anything is where it claims to be.

howItWorks.step: For ownership, it derives each story's tester by walking every story's child work items (via `Hierarchy-Forward` relations) and reading the `AssignedTo` of the child Task titled 'QA_Test Creation', building a storyId → tester map.
howItWorks.explain: Ownership isn't stored on the story directly — it lives on a child **Task**, so this walks the hierarchy to find it. For each story it pulls `Hierarchy-Forward` relations (parent → child), batch-fetches those children with only the four fields it needs, then scans for the one Task whose title contains `qa_test creation` and reads its `System.AssignedTo`. The `break` on first match makes that Task authoritative — later children aren't considered — and `System.AssignedTo` is an **identity object**, not a string, so it's run through `extractDisplayName` rather than used raw. Stories with no children, or none matching, are simply skipped, leaving them absent from the map.

howItWorks.step: For the audit, it walks every test case in a suite and flags three defects: no `TestedBy` link to its story, a reversed link, or a title that breaks the naming convention. Story ID is parsed from the title.
howItWorks.explain: The direction of a `TestedBy` link is the whole game. From a **test case's** side, the correct link to its story is `TestedBy-Reverse` (story is tested-by this case); `TestedBy-Forward` on a test case means someone linked it backwards. So `hasCorrectLink` checks Reverse, `hasWrongLink` checks Forward, and the two combine into distinct verdicts: neither present → `missingLink`, only the backwards one → `wrongLink`. All of this is gated on `storyId` being parseable from the title via `extractStoryIdFromTitle` — a title the parser can't read yields no story ID, so the case is left un-audited rather than falsely flagged. The naming check is independent: `!title.startsWith(correctPrefix)` (where `correctPrefix` is `TC_US<storyId>_`) sets `needsRename`, and any of the three defects pushes an issue.

howItWorks.step: It prints every defect first, then — only on approval — repairs the links and normalizes titles to the convention.
howItWorks.explain: This is a deterministic prefix-repair, ordered most-specific first. The early `startsWith(correctPrefix)` return is the idempotency guard — an already-correct title is returned untouched, which is what makes re-running safe. Then it strips known-wrong prefixes: a `TC_US<wrong-number>_` or `TC_UC<number>_` prefix (the `_?` allows the stray-underscore variant, `[\s_]` eats either a space or underscore separator) is **replaced** with the correct one, so the wrong story number is discarded rather than kept. A `US<number>_` title is only missing the `TC_` tag, so it's prepended, not replaced. The final fallback assumes no recognizable prefix at all and simply prepends `correctPrefix`, preserving the original descriptive text.

howItWorks.step: For a bulk reassignment (e.g. someone leaves), it updates three targets in order: the 'QA_Test Creation' Task's `AssignedTo`, each linked test case's `AssignedTo`, and the suite's test-point tester.
howItWorks.explain: Ownership in ADO lives in **three separate places**, and changing one doesn't touch the others — that's why the reassignment fans out. The Task and each test case are work items, so their `System.AssignedTo` is updated with a JSON-Patch `replace` op (`replace`, not `add`, because the field already holds a value). Test points are *not* work items — they belong to the Test Plan/suite and carry their own `tester` identity — so they go through the separate `updateTestPoints` API keyed by point ID, not work-item ID. The point update filters to only points whose `testCaseReference.id` is in `tcNewTester`, so points for cases outside this reassignment are left alone; miss step 3 and the plan's execution view would still show the old owner even after the work items were patched.

howItWorks.step: For filing, it adds test cases to the named suite in batches of 200, sleeping between batches to stay under ADO API rate limits.
howItWorks.explain: Two guardrails do the real work here. `Array.from(new Set(ids))` collapses duplicate IDs first, so a test case listed twice isn't added twice — and since adding an already-present case is a no-op in ADO, the whole operation stays idempotent. The `for` loop then slices the IDs into `BATCH_SIZE` (200) chunks and `sleep`s `BATCH_DELAY_MS` **between** batches — the `if (i + BATCH_SIZE < unique.length)` guard skips the pause after the final chunk, so it never sleeps needlessly. That throttle is deliberate: ADO rate-limits bulk suite writes, and firing hundreds of adds back-to-back risks HTTP 429s. The `dryRun` short-circuit returns before any write, making a preview truly read-only.

examples.caption: Audit a suite for link/naming defects
examples.input: Validate every test case in the 'Checkout Redesign' suite for bad links and off-convention titles — dry run.
examples.output: 24 clean. 3 defects: #211 has no TestedBy link, #214's link is reversed, and #217 is titled 'Login test 3' instead of the `TC_US..._` convention. Dry run — nothing written. Approve to fix.

examples.caption: Auto-assign testers from authorship
examples.input: For the 'Payments' feature, set each test case's owner to its author.
examples.output: Resolved 5 testers across 40 test cases from their 'QA_Test Creation' tasks. Set Alex on 12, Priya on 14, and so on — 40 `AssignedTo` updates, 0 errors.

examples.caption: Bulk-reassign when someone leaves
examples.input: Move all of story #305's tests from Sam to Jordan.
examples.output: Patched the authoring Task to Jordan, reassigned 9 test cases, and updated their 9 test points. Done.

underHood.heading: Resolving test ownership
underHood.whenRuns: When you assign owners or request a per-tester breakdown.
underHood.output: A storyId → tester map, read off each story's 'QA_Test Creation' Task `AssignedTo`.

underHood.heading: Auditing the suite
underHood.whenRuns: On a validate run, before any write.
underHood.input: Every test case currently in the suite.
underHood.output: A defect list: missing links, reversed links, and off-convention titles.

underHood.heading: Normalizing titles
underHood.whenRuns: Only after approval — never on a dry run.
underHood.input: A test case's current title and its story ID.

underHood.heading: Bulk reassignment
underHood.whenRuns: When ownership changes, e.g. someone leaves.
underHood.output: Three targets patched in order: the authoring Task, each test case's `AssignedTo`, and each test point's tester.

underHood.heading: Adding cases to a suite
underHood.whenRuns: When you add test cases, in batches of 200.
underHood.input: A list of test case IDs.
underHood.output: Those test cases appear in the target suite in ADO.

prerequisites: Node ≥ 18 and a terminal (macOS/Linux shell or Windows PowerShell).
Azure DevOps Test Plans access and a **PAT** scoped to edit work items and test points.
The Test Plan ID and suite ID you want to organize — both visible in the ADO URL when you open the suite.

steps.label: Install Node.js — the engine that runs the agent.
steps.cmd:
# macOS (with Homebrew):
brew install node

# or download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, then check it worked:
node -v   # should print v18 or higher
steps.why: The agent is TypeScript run under Node — a one-time per-machine install.

steps.label: Clone the agent and install its dependencies.
steps.why: `npm install` pulls the ADO client and xlsx reader into `node_modules`.
steps.firstRun: Cold install — a minute or two.

steps.label: Set the target org, project, and PAT (env vars).
steps.cmd:
export ADO_ORGANIZATION=my-org
export ADO_PROJECT="My Project"
export ADO_PAT=your-access-token
steps.why: Read at startup: which ADO org/project to hit and the PAT that authorizes the writes.

steps.label: Audit first with --dry-run.
steps.why: `--dry-run` prints every test case with a missing link, reversed link, or off-convention title, but writes nothing. Review the list before letting it write.
steps.firstRun: Reads every test case in the suite and reports defects.

steps.label: Approve by re-running without --dry-run.
steps.why: Same audit, but now it repairs the `TestedBy` links and normalizes the titles it flagged.
steps.rerun: Idempotent — anything already correct is skipped; only remaining defects get fixed.

inputs.name: --plan-id <id> --suite-id <id>
inputs.desc: Which Test Plan and suite to operate on.

inputs.name: --validate-links [--dry-run]
inputs.desc: Audits (and, without --dry-run, repairs) missing/reversed `TestedBy` links and off-convention titles.

inputs.name: --assign-testers / --reassign-map
inputs.desc: Sets or bulk-reassigns test case ownership to a tester.

inputs.name: --input <xlsx>
inputs.desc: A list of test case IDs to add to the suite.

outputs.name: console audit report
outputs.desc: Every defect found — missing link, reversed link, or off-convention title — with a before/after for each rename.

outputs.name: updated tracker items
outputs.desc: Once approved: the test case's `TestedBy` link and/or title corrected directly in ADO; no local file is produced.

runbook.rerun: Idempotent — every pass only reports (and, if approved, fixes) remaining defects; anything already correct is skipped, so the output shrinks as the backlog clears.
runbook.integrate: Run the `--dry-run` audit as a weekly health-check job and forward the report only when it's non-empty — a clean suite yields an empty report, which is itself useful signal.

video.caption: A 3-minute screen recording: audit a suite of test cases, then approve the fixes.
script: Open a terminal beside the tracker's folder view in a browser.
Say: 'This agent is the filing clerk for our test checklists. Let's audit one folder.'
Run `node -v` and `npm install` (or note it's already done); one line each on why.
Show the `export ADO_...` lines; say this is the only project-specific part.
Run the `--validate-links --dry-run` command; narrate the issues it lists — missing link, wrong direction, bad name.
Point at one flagged checklist in the browser tracker to show the problem is real.
Run the same command without `--dry-run`; watch it print 'linked' / 'renamed' per item.
Refresh the browser tracker to show the fixed title and link.
Mention in passing that the same agent also assigns testers and reassigns whole batches.
Close: 'Same command, safe to run weekly — it only touches what's still wrong.'
